import numpy as np
import rasterio
from rasterio.windows import from_bounds

NEPAL = {"west": 80.05, "south": 26.35, "east": 88.20, "north": 30.45}
SRC = "data/nepal_rangeland_image.tif"

with rasterio.open(SRC) as src:
    print(f"bands: {src.count}")
    print(f"dtypes: {src.dtypes}")
    print(f"extent: {src.bounds}")
    
    window = from_bounds(NEPAL["west"], NEPAL["south"],
                         NEPAL["east"], NEPAL["north"],
                         transform=src.transform)
    data = src.read(window=window)   # shape: (bands, H, W)
    
    print(f"\ncropped shape: {data.shape}")
    for i in range(src.count):
        band = data[i]
        uniq = np.unique(band)[:10]
        print(f"  band {i+1}: min={band.min()} max={band.max()} uniq={uniq}")
    
    # Sample a rangeland pixel
    if src.count >= 3:
        # Any pixel where R+G+B sums to non-zero
        nonzero = np.argwhere(data[:3].sum(axis=0) > 0)
        if len(nonzero):
            y, x = nonzero[len(nonzero) // 2]
            vals = [int(data[i, y, x]) for i in range(src.count)]
            print(f"\nsample rangeland pixel at ({y},{x}): {vals}")

import numpy as np
import rasterio
from rasterio.windows import from_bounds
from PIL import Image

NEPAL = {"west": 80.05, "south": 26.35, "east": 88.20, "north": 30.45}
SRC = "data/nepal_rangeland_image.tif"
OUT = "data/nepal_rangeland.png"

with rasterio.open(SRC) as src:
    window = from_bounds(NEPAL["west"], NEPAL["south"],
                         NEPAL["east"], NEPAL["north"],
                         transform=src.transform)
    b = rasterio.windows.bounds(window, src.transform)
    print(f"cropped bounds: west={b[0]:.4f} south={b[1]:.4f} "
          f"east={b[2]:.4f} north={b[3]:.4f}")

    raw = src.read(window=window)   # (bands, H, W)

    if src.count >= 4:
        # RGBA: use alpha channel as mask, copy RGB through
        rgb = raw[:3].transpose(1, 2, 0)          # (H, W, 3)
        mask = raw[3] > 0
    elif src.count == 3:
        # RGB: green-dominant = rangeland
        rgb = raw.transpose(1, 2, 0)
        r, g, bl = raw[0], raw[1], raw[2]
        mask = (g > 100) & (g > r) & (g > bl)
    else:
        # Single-band fallback
        data = raw[0]
        mask = data != 0
        rgb = np.zeros((*data.shape, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
        rgb[mask] = [56, 255, 30]

print(f"rangeland px: {mask.sum()} / {mask.size} "
      f"({mask.sum() / mask.size * 100:.2f}%)")

# Compose RGBA output: keep original RGB, set alpha from mask
rgba = np.zeros((*mask.shape, 4), dtype=np.uint8)
rgba[..., :3] = rgb
rgba[..., 3] = np.where(mask, 255, 0).astype(np.uint8)

Image.fromarray(rgba, mode="RGBA").save(OUT, optimize=True)
print(f"saved {OUT}")

title: Global Institute for Interdisciplinary Studies
text: The Global Institute for Interdisciplinary Studies (GIIS) is an educational institution based in Kathmandu, Nepal. GIIS promotes and conducts interdisciplinary research to generate credible, salient and legitimate knowledge that catalyzes a transformative change in the developmental policies and practices in Nepal and elsewhere. Through deep engagement with decision makers and multiple stakeholders, GIIS aims to shape developmental agenda that is socially-just, environmentally sustainable, and economically viable. Our interdisciplinary team has a strong track record of extensive research in Climate change and Landuse change, Natural resources and the Environment, Geohazards and Disasters, Society and Migration, Global health and Nutrition, Gender and Equality. Currently, we have 15 research fellows and our team is gradually expanding

title: Quarto + Closeread + Folium Story Map Site Improvement Checklist
text:
**Missing Closeread configuration in _quarto.yml**: The _quarto.yml doesn’t include specific configuration for the closeread-html format that’s used in your project files. This can affect how Closeread features are rendered.

Action: Add proper closeread-html configuration to _quarto.yml
Example: Add closeread-html: section with appropriate settings






Map performance optimization: The Python script that creates the map loads several large GeoJSON files and processes them in real-time, which could cause slow rendering on lower-end devices.

Action: Pre-process and cache map data where possible to improve load times
Example: Create a separate script for map generation with caching






Responsive design gaps: The CSS uses fixed heights (75vh) that might not work well on all devices or screen sizes.

Action: Add more responsive units like max-width and use clamp() for better scaling
Example: Replace height: 75vh with responsive units









Inconsistent Python code formatting: The Python script has inconsistent indentation and lacks proper docstrings/comments.

Action: Format the Python code with consistent indentation and add documentation
Example: Add function docstrings and improve code comments






Missing view transition feedback: The map navigation doesn’t provide clear visual feedback when changing views.

Action: Add loading indicators or visual cues during view transitions
Example: Add a “Loading…” overlay during view changes






Missing accessibility attributes: The HTML lacks accessibility features like ARIA labels for the map and interactive elements.

Action: Add proper ARIA labels and semantic HTML
Example: Add aria-label attributes to important elements






No error handling in Python script: If any of the GeoJSON files are missing or corrupted, the map generation will fail silently.

Action: Add try/catch blocks for file operations and data processing
Example: Wrap file loading operations with error handling









Missing project documentation: There’s no README or documentation explaining how to set up the environment and run the project.

Action: Create a README.md with setup instructions
Example: Add section on setting up the conda environment, installing dependencies, etc.






Map data loading optimization: The Python script loads all GeoJSON data each time without caching or optimization.

Action: Implement data caching and pre-processing steps for better performance
Example: Save processed GeoJSON to intermediate files that can be reused






Limited map layer controls: The map has many layers but no user-friendly controls to toggle them on/off.

Action: Add a layer control panel or similar interface
Example: Implement a layer control UI for users to interact with different map layers






Mobile-specific CSS issues: Some CSS rules might not work optimally on mobile devices.

Action: Add media queries for mobile optimization
Example: Add @media queries to adjust spacing and sizing for smaller screens

title: Rangelands in Change
text:
Rangelands in Change
Vegetation trends, pastoral livelihoods and pathways for management​ in Nepal.  















Rangelands span diverse ecosystems, including grasslands, savannas, shrublands, and alpine pastures shaped by fluctuating rainfall, temperature swings, and broader climate variability alongside soil conditions and grazing management. They cover roughly 13% of Earth’s terrestrial surface, totaling 15,000,000 km² out of land area.Source: Gong et al. (2012)




Rangelands provide a wide range of ecosystem services including forage, water, carbon storage, biodiversity habitat, and cultural value.






Yarsagumba (top left), Wool (top right), Churpi (bottom left), Woman milking a Yak (bottom right)





Distribution Nepal’s rangelands span the high-altitude Trans-Himalayan belt down to the mid-hills, covering critical ecological and pastoral gradients.Nationally, they support extensive livestock production and wildlife corridors. 2.1 M haTotal rangeland area14%of Nepal




Climate Change Content.




Content.




The Karnali Province Karnali Province, the largest province in Nepal, is home to diverse rangeland ecosystems. These areas are vital for local livelihoods, supporting pastoral communities and serving as habitats for endemic species.




Mapping Rangelands We used participatory mapping approach to map all the rangelands in Jumla district and 4 municipalities in the Dolpa district.




Our Ecological Survey and Restoration Sites Rangelands We conducted field surveys across various rangeland sites of Jumla and Dolpa districts in Karnali, focusing on vegetation composition, soil health, grazing patterns. Furthermore we did couple of rangeland restoration projects.
